title: Canaryed Entitlements Deploy Playbook and SIEM Mapping
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a pragmatic, engineering-facing playbook for rolling out RBAC v2 entitlements using a canary-first approach that tightly couples permission rollout with automated evidence collection and SIEM-friendly audit exports. The goal is to reduce blast radius from permission changes, capture verifiable evidence for every change, and make the telemetry consumable by downstream threat-detection processes without heavy post-processing.

Audience:
- Security engineers owning entitlement platform
- SRE/Infra who run the rollout pipelines
- Product/Platform engineers who ship permission changes
- SOC analysts who consume SIEM artifacts

High-level goals (measurable):
- No high-severity privilege regressions in canary cohort (target: 0 incidents)
- Evidence bundles for 100% of canary permission deltas (target: 100%)
- SIEM export latency <= 60s for audit events from canary cohorts
- Rollback window automated (< 5 minutes to initiate)

Key assumptions and constraints:
- RBAC v2 model supports time-bound grants and cohort-scoped grants (already deployed in platform API).
- We have an evidence-store (S3-backed) with pre-signed URLs and tamper-evident signing.
- SIEM accepts NDJSON line-delimited events over a secure ingest endpoint and can index flat fields efficiently.
- Canary cohorts are at most 2% of user population and grouped by tenant (customer) when applicable.

Definitions (working):
- Canaryed Entitlement: a permission change applied only to a small, observable cohort.
- Evidence Bundle: signed artifact containing the change diffs, test run outputs, authz-sim logs, and operator intent note.
- Audit Event: single flat record per permission-check or grant-change emitted to SIEM.

Playbook overview (phases):
1) Preparation and prechecks (dev/staging):
   - Author creates a permission delta PR in the authorization repo. PR must include: change diff (human readable), rationale, test-plan, smoke-eval prompt set, and SLOs for the change.
   - Automation kicks off a validation job: static lint, policy-compat checks, and offline simulation against a 10k-sample of historical access paths.
   - If validation fails, PR auto-blocks merge. Add a short operator note with remediation steps.

2) Canary deploy (controlled):
   - Merge occurs into main but change is gated by the rollout controller. Controller exposes canary flags: cohort-id, cohort-size, start-time, auto-rollback-thresholds.
   - Create Evidence Bundle automatically at the moment the change is scheduled. Evidence bundle components:
     - delta.json (permission diff),
     - sim-results.txt (results from offline sim),
     - smoke-run.log (end-to-end smoke tests),
     - operator-note.md (free-text),
     - signature.sig (crypto signature of the bundle)
   - Upload bundle to evidence-store and include signed reference id in the SIEM events for traceability.

3) Observability and gating during canary:
   - Emit high-fidelity audit events for every decision point for entities within the cohort. Events are exported in near real-time to SIEM (<=60s).
   - Key canary gating metrics to monitor (real-time dashboards):
     - Authorization-deny-rate delta (cohort vs baseline)
     - Error rate on authz-service (5xxs and timeouts)
     - Unexpected-allow incidents (detected by smoke prompts)
     - Latency p95 for permission checks
   - Automated gates: if deny-rate delta > 1.5x baseline OR unexpected-allow incidents > 0 OR authz 5xx increase > 0.5%, controller auto-rolls back and flags SOC.

4) Rollforward / full rollout:
   - If canary holds for the monitoring window (default 24 hours, configurable), perform staged increment (2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%). At each step create an incremental Evidence Bundle.

Rollback and forensic path:
- Automatic rollback: controller triggers reverse change and attaches rollback-evidence bundle.
- Forensics: Evidence bundles are immutable and indexable by bundle-id. SOC and SRE can pull bundle and replay sim runs locally.

SIEM audit export schema (flat, index-friendly):
- We intentionally keep fields flat and small to make SIEM indexing predictable. Example fields to include on every audit event (NDJSON line per event):
    event_time: ISO8601 timestamp (string)
    event_type: "permission-check" | "grant-change" | "rollback" | "evidence-upload" (string)
    request_id: unique request id (string)
    trace_id: trace id (string)
    actor_id: principal id (string)
    actor_type: "user" | "service" | "admin" (string)
    actor_roles_before: comma-separated short role ids (string)
    actor_roles_after: comma-separated short role ids or empty (string)
    resource_type: e.g., "model", "project", "dataset" (string)
    resource_id: short resource id (string)
    action: e.g., "read", "write", "deploy" (string)
    outcome: "allow" | "deny" | "error" (string)
    policy_version: semantic ref like "authz-v2@2026-02-01" (string)
    change_delta_id: evidence bundle id for grant-change or rollback (string)
    canary_cohort: cohort id or empty (string)
    latency_ms: integer as string (e.g., "23")
    error_code: short error tag or empty (string)
    agent_env: staging|canary|prod (string)
    signature_ref: signed evidence pointer when applicable (string)

Sample NDJSON line (literal example):
{"event_time":"2026-02-27T14:12:03Z","event_type":"permission-check","request_id":"req_4d7f9","trace_id":"trace_a1b2","actor_id":"user:12345","actor_type":"user","actor_roles_before":"reader,analytics","actor_roles_after":"reader,analytics","resource_type":"project","resource_id":"proj-88","action":"read","outcome":"allow","policy_version":"authz-v2@2026-02-01","change_delta_id":"","canary_cohort":"cohort-17","latency_ms":"12","error_code":"","agent_env":"canary","signature_ref":"evidence://bundles/b-20260227-17.sig"}

Event sampling and cardinality considerations:
- We do NOT emit full actor role arrays as nested objects; we compress into CSV strings to limit field cardinality.
- For high-volume paths (token-generation API for hosted customers), switch to sampled-event export with higher sampling-rate for canary cohorts (100%) and lower for baseline (1%). Always emit grant-change and evidence-upload events at 100%.

Evidence automation contract (minimal):
- On merge-to-main + schedule: platform creates bundle and returns bundle-id.
- Authorization service attaches bundle-id to any grant-change event and provides pre-signed evidence_store_url.
- Rollout-controller enriches SIEM events with canary_cohort and policy_version.
- Evidence-store exposes immutable GETs and an audit log for retrieval (signed by evidence signer).

Operational runbook (short):
- If SIEM shows unexpected-allow incidents: pause rollout, pull evidence bundle, run targeted sim with failing prompt set, escalate to owner.
- If authz latency regression observed: throttle rollout immediately and open infra incident.
- If evidence upload fails: halt canary and retry upload; if persistent, abort and roll back.

Checklist before authorizing a canary:
- [ ] PR has smoke prompts and expected outcomes
- [ ] Offline sim run attached and green
- [ ] Evidence bundle produced and accessible
- [ ] Canary cohort defined and size validated
- [ ] Dashboards created and alerts configured (deny-rate, unexpected-allow, latency)
- [ ] Auto-rollback thresholds set and tested in staging

Follow-ups and open questions:
- Should we version the SIEM field set as a schema (e.g., siem-schema-v1) in the event payload to allow evolution? Recommendation: yes — include schema_version field when we bump fields.
- Long-term: evaluate compressing actor role snapshots with a role-hash pointer rather than CSV to reduce cardinality; will require SIEM lookup table support.

Appendix: quick automation snippets (operator notes)
- Evidence bundle CLI (example):
  rbw evidence create --delta pr-1234 --sim sim-out.txt --smoke smoke.log --note "Canary for dataset-read-fix" --sign > bundle-id
  rbw rollout schedule --bundle bundle-id --cohort cohort-17 --size 0.02 --autopause-on "deny_delta>1.5x"

- Quick SIEM query to find canary-related denies in last 15m:
  index=authz_events event_type=permission-check canary_cohort=* outcome=deny | stats count by actor_id, resource_type

End of playbook.

Notes: This is intentionally operational and prescriptive rather than purely theoretical. If reviewers want more formal schema docs, we can extract a delta-spec and a Confluence-formatted schema file and lock the schema versioning contract.
